title: Repository Guidelines
text: - mail-like layer lets coding agents coordinate asynchronously via MCP tools resources. - Provides identities, inbox/outbox, searchable threads, advisory file reservations, human-auditable artifacts Git. ’s useful - Prevents agents stepping explicit file reservations (leases) files/globs. - Keeps communication token budget storing messages per-project archive. - Offers quick reads (resource://inbox/..., resource://thread/...) macros bundle common flows. use effectively 1) repository - Register identity: call ensure_project, register_agent using repo’s absolute path project_key. - Reserve files edit: file_reservation_paths(project_key, agent_name, ["src/**"], ttl_seconds=3600, exclusive=true) signal intent avoid conflict. - Communicate threads: use send_message(..., thread_id="FEAT-123"); check inbox fetch_inbox acknowledge acknowledge_message. - Read fast: resource://inbox/{Agent}?project=<abs-path>&limit=20 resource://thread/{id}?project=<abs-path>&include_bodies=true. - Tip: set AGENT_NAME environment pre-commit guard can block commits conflict others’ active exclusive file reservations. Option (single project bus): register sides project_key (shared key/path). Keep reservation patterns specific (e.g., frontend/** vs backend/**). Option B (separate projects): repo project_key; use macro_contact_handshake request_contact/respond_contact link agents, message directly. Keep shared thread_id (e.g., ticket key) across repos clean summaries/audits. Macros vs granular tools - Prefer macros want speed smaller model: macro_start_session, macro_prepare_thread, macro_file_reservation_cycle, macro_contact_handshake. - Use granular tools need control: register_agent, file_reservation_paths, send_message, fetch_inbox, acknowledge_message. Common pitfalls - “from_agent registered”: always register_agent correct project_key first. - “FILE_RESERVATION_CONFLICT”: adjust patterns, wait expiry, use non-exclusive reservation appropriate. - Auth errors: JWT+JWKS enabled, include bearer token kid matches server JWKS; static bearer used JWT disabled.

title: Displaying Surfaces with RGL
text: Surface curvature helps distinguish gyri (outward folds) sulci (inward folds). curvature() function calculates , curv_cols_smooth() maps values continuous grayscale gradient (dark sulci, light gyri) natural-looking shading. simpler binary split, see curv_cols(). Either way, pass resulting colors bgcol argument plot().
code: # Calculate curvature colors curv_colors <- curv_cols_smooth(curv_lh_display)  # Plot with curvature background from a medial viewpoint render_surface(white_lh_display, bgcol = curv_colors, viewpoint = "medial", specular = "black")

title: Displaying Surfaces with RGL
text: Often, want visualize data mapped onto surface vertices (e.g., activation values, thickness). can pass vector values vals argument. cmap argument specifies color map, irange defines data range map onto colormap. Values outside irange clamped minimum maximum color.
code: # Overlay random data using a rainbow colormap # Map data range from -2 to 2 onto the colormap render_surface(white_lh_display, vals = random_vals_display_smooth, cmap = rainbow(256),                irange = c(-2, 2), thresh = NULL, viewpoint = "lateral", specular = "gray")

title: Displaying Surfaces with RGL
text: thresh argument (vector two values, c(lower, upper)) can used vals make parts surface transparent. Vertices corresponding value vals inside range (lower upper) rendered transparently; values outside remain opaque. useful masking band values.
code: # Same data overlay as above, but make values between -1 and 1 transparent render_surface(white_lh_display, vals = random_vals_display_smooth, cmap = rainbow(256),                irange = c(-2, 2), thresh = c(-1, 1), viewpoint = "lateral", lit = TRUE)

title: Displaying Surfaces with RGL
text: Instead mapping data values colormap, can provide vector specific hex color codes directly vert_clrs argument. overrides vals cmap. vector length must match number vertices.
code: # Color vertices based on their x-coordinate (e.g., red for positive x, blue for negative) x_coords <- coords(white_lh_display)[, 1] vertex_colors <- ifelse(x_coords > median(x_coords), "#FF0000", "#0000FF") # Red/Blue  render_surface(white_lh_display, vert_clrs = vertex_colors, viewpoint = "ventral", lit = TRUE)

title: Displaying Surfaces with RGL
text: alpha argument controls overall transparency surface, ranging 0 (fully transparent) 1 (fully opaque).
code: # Plot the surface with 60% opacity (40% transparent) render_surface(white_lh_display, vals = random_vals_display_smooth, cmap = heat.colors(256),                irange = c(-2, 2), alpha = 0.6, viewpoint = "posterior")

title: Displaying Surfaces with RGL
text: appearance surface affected lighting. specular argument controls color specular highlights (shininess). Setting "black" creates matte appearance.
code: # Plot with a matte finish (no specular highlights) render_surface(white_lh_display, vals = random_vals_display_smooth, cmap = topo.colors(256),                irange = c(-2, 2), specular = "black", viewpoint = "lateral", lit = TRUE)

code: # Smooth the right hemisphere and get its curvature white_rh_smooth <- smooth(white_rh, type = "HCLaplace", delta = 0.2, iteration = 5) curv_rh <- curvature(white_rh_smooth)  # Try snapshot approach for two hemispheres .render_counter$n <- .render_counter$n + 1 two_hemi_file <- knitr::fig_path(paste0("-twohemi-", .render_counter$n, ".png")) dir.create(dirname(two_hemi_file), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)  img_path <- try({   file <- two_hemi_file   rgl::open3d()   rgl::par3d(windowRect = c(0, 0, 1200, 600))   rgl::bg3d(color = "white")    # Plot LH with curvature background    view_surface(white_lh_display, bgcol = curv_cols_smooth(curv_lh_display),                viewpoint = "lateral", new_window = FALSE)   # Plot RH offset to the right   view_surface(white_rh_smooth, bgcol = curv_cols_smooth(curv_rh),                viewpoint = "lateral", new_window = FALSE, offset = c(100, 0, 0))   # Zoom out so both hemispheres are visible   rgl::view3d(fov = 0, zoom = 0.35,               userMatrix = rbind(c(0,-1,0,0), c(0,0,1,0), c(-1,0,0,0), c(0,0,0,1)))    if (rgl::rgl.useNULL() && requireNamespace("webshot2", quietly = TRUE)) {     rgl::snapshot3d(file, webshot = TRUE)   } else {     rgl::rgl.snapshot(file)   }   rgl::close3d()   file }, silent = TRUE)  if (!inherits(img_path, "try-error") && file.exists(img_path)) {   knitr::include_graphics(img_path) } else {   # Fallback to rglwidget   rgl::open3d()   view_surface(white_lh_display, bgcol = curv_cols_smooth(curv_lh_display),                viewpoint = "lateral", new_window = FALSE)   view_surface(white_rh_smooth, bgcol = curv_cols_smooth(curv_rh),                viewpoint = "lateral", new_window = FALSE, offset = c(100, 0, 0))   rgl::view3d(fov = 0, zoom = 0.35,               userMatrix = rbind(c(0,-1,0,0), c(0,0,1,0), c(-1,0,0,0), c(0,0,0,1)))   rgl::rglwidget() }

title: Surfplot-style Figures with neurosurf
text: package ships decimated fsaverage surfaces (std.8). use white pial surfaces project Schaefer atlas MNI152 volume space surface, inflated surfaces visualization. example assume Schaefer 200-parcel, 7-network atlas MNI152 space available inst/extdata. use neuroim2 load volume vol_to_surf() map parcel labels surface vertices. helper vol_to_surf() returns NeuroSurface per-vertex labels mapping geometry. extract labels reuse inflated plotting geometry simple concatenation.
code: # Geometry for plotting fs_infl <- load_fsaverage_std8("inflated") lh <- fs_infl$lh rh <- fs_infl$rh  # White / pial surfaces for volume-to-surface mapping lh_white <- read_surf_geometry(   system.file("extdata", "std.8_lh.white.asc", package = "neurosurf") ) lh_pial <- read_surf_geometry(   system.file("extdata", "std.8_lh.pial.asc", package = "neurosurf") ) rh_white <- read_surf_geometry(   system.file("extdata", "std.8_rh.white.asc", package = "neurosurf") ) rh_pial <- read_surf_geometry(   system.file("extdata", "std.8_rh.pial.asc", package = "neurosurf") ) atlas_path <- system.file(   "extdata",   "Schaefer2018_200Parcels_7Networks_order_FSLMNI152_1mm.nii.gz",   package = "neurosurf" )  if (atlas_path != "") {   atlas_img <- neuroim2::read_vol(atlas_path)    # Project volume labels to surface vertices (mode of nearby voxels)   lh_labels <- vol_to_surf(lh_white, lh_pial, atlas_img, fun = "mode")   rh_labels <- vol_to_surf(rh_white, rh_pial, atlas_img, fun = "mode") } else {   warning("Schaefer atlas file not found in extdata; using placeholder zeros for vignette build.")   lh_labels <- NeuroSurface(lh_white, indices = seq_len(length(nodes(lh_white))),                             data = integer(length(nodes(lh_white))))   rh_labels <- NeuroSurface(rh_white, indices = seq_len(length(nodes(rh_white))),                             data = integer(length(nodes(rh_white)))) } lh_parcels <- lh_labels@data rh_parcels <- rh_labels@data  # Combine into a single vector for add_surface_layer() parcel_labels <- c(lh_parcels, rh_parcels)

text: **Coloring:** Surface vertex colors determined following priority:   1. `vert_clrs`: provided, specific hex colors used.   2. `vals` & `cmap`: `vals` provided `vert_clrs` NULL, `vals` mapped `cmap` based `irange`.   3. `bgcol`: neither `vert_clrs` `vals` used coloring, `bgcol` applied uniformly.   `bgcol` specified alongside `vert_clrs` `vals`, colors blended based `alpha` parameter. **Transparency:** Overall transparency set `alpha`. Additional threshold-based   transparency can applied using `thresh` `vals` provided. Vertices   values outside `thresh` range become fully transparent. **Lighting:** `add_normals=TRUE` recommended realistic lighting. `specular`   parameter controls shininess. **Viewpoint:** Predefined viewpoints (`"lateral"`, `"medial"`, etc.) automatically   adjusted based hemisphere specified `surfgeom@hemi` (e.g., "lh" results   "left_lateral"). `hemi` unknown, current `rgl` view used unless   custom 4x4 matrix provided. **Performance:** Rendering large surfaces surfaces complex coloring/transparency   can computationally intensive.
